title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 5 questions (5.1, 5.2, 5.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A payroll vendor can only drop a nightly CSV export on a file share and offers no API. The team wants the data in Identity Security Cloud as soon as possible. Which source type is the BEST fit?
choices: A JDBC source that queries the file share
A delimited file source loaded from the export
A Web Services source with a GET operation
An Active Directory source with a custom schema
questions.answer: A delimited file source loaded from the export
questions.explanation: A delimited file source loads accounts from an uploaded CSV, which suits a system with only a file export. JDBC needs a database to query, not a file share.

questions.stem: A cloud application has a documented REST API but no prebuilt SailPoint connector. The engineer needs aggregation and provisioning. Which connector should the engineer configure?
choices: JDBC, with a SQL query for each action
Delimited File, with a scheduled upload
Web Services, with HTTP operations for each action
Active Directory, with a custom object type
questions.answer: Web Services, with HTTP operations for each action
questions.explanation: The Web Services connector calls REST endpoints through configured HTTP operations such as account aggregation and create account. JDBC only talks to databases.

questions.stem: A company with no on-premises data center wants to connect a SaaS application that has a SailPoint SaaS connector. What is true about where that connector runs?
choices: It runs on a virtual appliance that the company must deploy
It runs on an IQService host inside the company network
It runs in the application vendor's tenant as a plug-in
It runs in the SailPoint cloud and needs no virtual appliance
questions.answer: It runs in the SailPoint cloud and needs no virtual appliance
questions.explanation: SaaS connectors are cloud-native and run on SailPoint's platform, so no VA is needed. VA-based connectors are the ones that need an appliance near the target.

questions.stem: An in-house application keeps its users and roles in tables of an on-premises Oracle database. Which design BEST connects it to Identity Security Cloud?
choices: A JDBC source served by a VA cluster that can reach the database
A Web Services source called directly from the SailPoint cloud
A delimited file source fed by a manual export
A SaaS connector that reads the tables over the internet
questions.answer: A JDBC source served by a VA cluster that can reach the database
questions.explanation: A JDBC source runs on a VA, which reaches the private database and sends results to the tenant. A manual export would lose direct aggregation and provisioning.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a direct connection source and a flat file source?
choices: A direct source always needs a service desk; a flat file source never does
A direct source cannot be authoritative; a flat file source can
A direct source reads and writes the target through a connector; a flat file source is loaded from files
A direct source stores data on the VA; a flat file source stores it in the tenant
questions.answer: A direct source reads and writes the target through a connector; a flat file source is loaded from files
questions.explanation: Direct connectors aggregate from and provision to the target system. Flat file sources load from uploaded files, and both kinds can be authoritative.

questions.stem: A flat file source has no service desk integration attached. A user's access request for an entitlement on that source is approved. What happens next?
choices: The entitlement is written to the CSV file automatically
A manual work item is created for the source owner to fulfill
The request fails because flat file sources are read only
The VA connects to the application and adds the entitlement
questions.answer: A manual work item is created for the source owner to fulfill
questions.explanation: With no connector or service desk, ISC raises a manual task for the source owner. Nothing writes back to the uploaded file.

questions.stem: An engineer is onboarding Workday. A colleague suggests building a Web Services source against the Workday API instead of using the prebuilt connector. What is the BEST recommendation?
choices: Use the prebuilt connector, which already handles the vendor's API and schema
Build the Web Services source, because prebuilt connectors cannot be authoritative
Use a delimited file source, because HR sources should not be direct
Use JDBC against Workday's database for better performance
questions.answer: Use the prebuilt connector, which already handles the vendor's API and schema
questions.explanation: A supported prebuilt connector covers the vendor API, paging and schema, which lowers build and maintenance effort. Prebuilt connectors can be authoritative.

questions.stem: An engineer is planning a new Active Directory source for an on-premises forest. Which component must be in place first?
choices: A SaaS connector registered in the forest root domain
A ServiceNow integration that relays LDAP calls
An inbound firewall rule from the SailPoint cloud to each domain controller
A VA cluster with network access to the domain controllers
questions.answer: A VA cluster with network access to the domain controllers
questions.explanation: The AD connector runs on a VA that reaches the domain controllers and sends results outbound to the tenant. The cloud never connects inbound to the DCs.

questions.stem: Identity Security Cloud must set and reset Active Directory passwords. Which connection setting is required?
choices: Use the Global Catalog port for all password operations
Use SSL so the connector talks to the domain controllers over LDAPS
Use plain LDAP on port 389 with a stronger service account
Use a delimited file to send new passwords to the help desk
questions.answer: Use SSL so the connector talks to the domain controllers over LDAPS
questions.explanation: Active Directory accepts password changes only over an encrypted connection, so the source needs SSL (LDAPS). A stronger account does not encrypt the traffic.

questions.stem: A domain has four domain controllers. The engineer wants aggregation to keep working when one is down for patching. What should the engineer configure?
choices: List several domain controllers in the domain's server settings
Add a second VA cluster that points to the same controller
Lower the account deletion threshold for the source
Point the source at the Global Catalog port only
questions.answer: List several domain controllers in the domain's server settings
questions.explanation: Listing several servers lets the connector use another domain controller when one is unreachable. A second cluster aimed at the same DC still fails when that DC is down.

questions.stem: A forest has a root domain and two child domains. Accounts aggregate, but memberships in universal groups from other domains are missing. What is the MOST likely gap?
choices: The account deletion threshold is set too low
The source uses LDAPS instead of plain LDAP
The forest's Global Catalog server is not configured on the source
The identity profile uses the wrong priority
questions.answer: The forest's Global Catalog server is not configured on the source
questions.explanation: Cross-domain and universal group data is resolved through the Global Catalog, so the forest settings need a GC server. LDAPS only affects encryption.

questions.stem: New AD accounts must also get an Exchange mailbox and a home directory on a file server. What does the design need besides the AD source?
choices: A second AD source dedicated to Exchange
A cloud rule that SailPoint runs in the tenant
A JDBC source pointed at the Exchange database
IQService installed on a Windows server and configured on the source
questions.answer: IQService installed on a Windows server and configured on the source
questions.explanation: IQService runs on a Windows host and performs native tasks such as mailbox and home directory creation for the AD connector. A cloud rule cannot reach on-premises servers.

questions.stem: A firewall team asks which ports to open from the VAs for an AD source that uses SSL to the domain controllers and to the Global Catalog. Which ports should the engineer request?
choices: TCP 389 and TCP 3268
TCP 443 and TCP 8443
TCP 1433 and TCP 1521
TCP 636 and TCP 3269
questions.answer: TCP 636 and TCP 3269
questions.explanation: LDAPS uses 636 and the Global Catalog over SSL uses 3269. Ports 389 and 3268 are the unencrypted versions.

questions.stem: Security objects to a Domain Admin service account for the AD source, which aggregates and provisions users in two OUs. What is the BEST design?
choices: Keep Domain Admin but rotate the password weekly
Use a personal admin account so changes are traceable
Delegate only the needed rights on the target OUs to a dedicated account
Give the account read-only rights and accept failed provisioning
questions.answer: Delegate only the needed rights on the target OUs to a dedicated account
questions.explanation: Least privilege means delegating create, modify and delete rights only where ISC provisions. Rotating a Domain Admin password keeps excessive rights.

questions.stem: Only users under the Employees OU should be aggregated from a large domain. What is the BEST way to scope the source?
choices: Aggregate everything and delete extra accounts in ISC
Set the account search DN to the Employees OU
Add a transform that blanks accounts outside the OU
Raise the account deletion threshold for the source
questions.answer: Set the account search DN to the Employees OU
questions.explanation: The search DN limits which containers the connector reads, so out-of-scope accounts are never sent. Deleting them after aggregation would bring them back next run.

questions.stem: Computer objects are showing up as accounts on an AD source. Which setting should the engineer change?
choices: The iterate search filter, to return only person user objects
The group search DN, to exclude computer groups
The account correlation, to skip computer names
The Global Catalog port, to avoid machine accounts
questions.answer: The iterate search filter, to return only person user objects
questions.explanation: The iterate search filter is an LDAP filter on the account search, such as one that requires objectCategory=person. Correlation does not stop objects from being aggregated.

questions.stem: Entitlement aggregation brings in thousands of distribution and legacy groups. The business only governs groups in the App Groups OU. What should the engineer configure?
choices: An account search DN that points to the App Groups OU
A group search DN that points to the App Groups OU
A role that removes the unwanted groups
A lifecycle state that hides the unwanted groups
questions.answer: A group search DN that points to the App Groups OU
questions.explanation: The group search scope controls which groups become entitlements. The account search DN controls user objects, not groups.

questions.stem: Accounts show memberships of every group in the domain, but the team only wants memberships of groups in the Managed Groups OU. Which setting fits BEST?
choices: Group membership search DN set to the Managed Groups OU
Account search scope set to one level
Iterate search filter set to (objectClass=group)
Account deletion threshold set to zero
questions.answer: Group membership search DN set to the Managed Groups OU
questions.explanation: The group membership search DN limits which group memberships are read for accounts. An objectClass=group filter on the account search would return no users.

questions.stem: Users in nested OUs under the configured search DN are missing after aggregation, while users directly in that OU appear. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The Global Catalog is configured on the source
The service account can write to the OU
The search scope is one level instead of subtree
The source uses delta aggregation
questions.answer: The search scope is one level instead of subtree
questions.explanation: A one-level scope reads only the direct children of the DN, so nested OUs are skipped. Subtree includes every level below it.

questions.stem: An AD source uses delta aggregation. Over the weekend, IT reorganized users into new OUs. What should the engineer do?
choices: Keep delta aggregation, which tracks OU moves
Lower the deletion threshold to block the changes
Re-run entitlement aggregation only
Run a full account aggregation after the OU moves
questions.answer: Run a full account aggregation after the OU moves
questions.explanation: Delta aggregation does not support OU moves, which can cause unexpected results such as duplicate accounts. A full aggregation brings the accounts up to date.

questions.stem: Delta aggregation on an AD source fails with an access error while full aggregation works. Which permission does the service account MOST likely lack?
choices: Reset Password on the target OUs
Local administrator on the VA
Write access to the Global Catalog
Replicating Directory Changes on the domain
questions.answer: Replicating Directory Changes on the domain
questions.explanation: AD delta aggregation reads changes through the directory synchronization control, which needs the Replicating Directory Changes right. Reset Password is for provisioning, not reading changes.

questions.stem: Which connection URL format is correct for a JDBC source that reads a Microsoft SQL Server database named HR?
choices: ldap://dbhost:1433/databaseName=HR
https://dbhost:1433/HR?driver=jdbc
jdbc:sqlserver://dbhost:1433;databaseName=HR
sqlserver://dbhost/HR;protocol=jdbc
questions.answer: jdbc:sqlserver://dbhost:1433;databaseName=HR
questions.explanation: JDBC URLs start with jdbc: and the vendor prefix, here jdbc:sqlserver with host, port and databaseName. The other forms are not JDBC URLs.

questions.stem: Test Connection on a new JDBC source fails with "No suitable driver found". What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The service account password has expired
The driver for that database is missing or the URL prefix does not match it
The account SQL query returns too many rows
The VA cluster has only one appliance
questions.answer: The driver for that database is missing or the URL prefix does not match it
questions.explanation: That message means no loaded driver accepts the URL, so the driver JAR is missing or the URL prefix is wrong. A bad password gives a login error instead.

questions.stem: A JDBC source for MySQL fails with a ClassNotFoundException for the driver class. What should the engineer do?
choices: Upload the vendor's JDBC driver JAR to the source
Change the account SQL query to use a view
Turn on delta aggregation for the source
Add the database host to the identity profile
questions.answer: Upload the vendor's JDBC driver JAR to the source
questions.explanation: The class cannot be found because the driver JAR is not present for the connector. Changing the query does not load a driver.

questions.stem: A JDBC source can reach the database from an engineer's laptop but Test Connection times out from the tenant. Where should the engineer look FIRST?
choices: The identity profile mappings for the source
The access profiles that use the source
The browser that ran Test Connection
Network access from the source's VAs to the database port
questions.answer: Network access from the source's VAs to the database port
questions.explanation: The JDBC connector runs on the VAs, so the database must be reachable from them, not from a laptop. Identity profiles play no part in connectivity.

questions.stem: A DBA is creating the account for a read-only JDBC source. Which approach follows least privilege BEST?
choices: Grant the database owner role for easier troubleshooting
Grant SELECT on a view that exposes only the needed columns
Reuse the application's own admin account
Grant SELECT on every table in the database
questions.answer: Grant SELECT on a view that exposes only the needed columns
questions.explanation: A view with only needed columns limits both rights and data sent to the cloud. Owner or admin rights go far beyond reading accounts.

questions.stem: Which driver class name belongs in a JDBC source that connects to Microsoft SQL Server?
choices: com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver
oracle.jdbc.driver.OracleDriver
com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver
org.postgresql.Driver
questions.answer: com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver
questions.explanation: SQL Server's Microsoft driver class is com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver. The others are the Oracle, MySQL and PostgreSQL drivers.

questions.stem: A JDBC source reads five million rows, and one aggregation runs for hours. What design change can speed it up?
choices: Add more identity attributes to the identity profile
Switch the source to a delimited file upload
Enable partitioning with statements that split the rows into ranges
Lower the percentage of deleted accounts allowed
questions.answer: Enable partitioning with statements that split the rows into ranges
questions.explanation: Partitioned aggregation runs several SQL statements in parallel, each covering part of the data. A delimited file would lose direct connectivity and not be faster.

questions.stem: A JDBC account query returns one row per account and group, but each account ends up with only one entitlement. What should the engineer fix?
choices: Mark the group column as the account's display attribute
Merge rows on the account identity column and sort the query by it
Run entitlement aggregation twice in a row
Change the source to a SaaS connector
questions.answer: Merge rows on the account identity column and sort the query by it
questions.explanation: To build multi-valued attributes, the connector merges consecutive rows for the same account, so results must be sorted by that column. Running more aggregations does not merge rows.

questions.stem: Helpdesk staff use Aggregate Account on single JDBC accounts. Which setting supports fetching one account?
choices: A group SQL query that returns every group
A delta table for the whole source
A second identity profile for the source
A get object SQL query that uses the account identity placeholder
questions.answer: A get object SQL query that uses the account identity placeholder
questions.explanation: Single-account aggregation uses the get object query, which selects one row using the account's identity value. The group query is for entitlements.

questions.stem: A JDBC source aggregates correctly, but approved access requests never change the database. What is the source MOST likely missing?
choices: A correlation rule for the account schema
A get object query for single accounts
A JDBC provision rule that writes the changes
A second VA in the source's cluster
questions.answer: A JDBC provision rule that writes the changes
questions.explanation: The JDBC connector provisions through a JDBC provision connector rule, which SailPoint reviews and deploys. Correlation rules only link accounts to identities.

questions.stem: Groups from a database should be requestable as entitlements with descriptions. What does the JDBC source need?
choices: A group query plus an entitlement attribute in the account schema
An access profile created before any aggregation
A role with membership criteria on each group
A delimited file with every group listed
questions.answer: A group query plus an entitlement attribute in the account schema
questions.explanation: Entitlement aggregation needs a group query, and the account schema attribute holding groups must be marked as an entitlement. Access profiles are built from entitlements, not before them.

questions.stem: An engineer is choosing the account ID column for a JDBC schema. Which column is the BEST choice?
choices: An email address that changes when people marry
An employee number that is unique and never changes
A display name that may repeat
A department code shared by many users
questions.answer: An employee number that is unique and never changes
questions.explanation: The account ID must be unique and stable, or renames look like a delete and a new account. Email and names can change or repeat.

questions.stem: An engineer enables delta aggregation on a JDBC source, but every run still reads all rows. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: JDBC sources never support delta aggregation
Delta aggregation only works on authoritative sources
Delta aggregation requires a delimited file
JDBC delta aggregation needs extra configuration to track changed rows
questions.answer: JDBC delta aggregation needs extra configuration to track changed rows
questions.explanation: JDBC does support delta aggregation, but it needs additional configuration so the connector knows which rows changed. Turning on the toggle alone is not enough.

questions.stem: An engineer is onboarding an on-premises database through a JDBC source. Put the steps in order.
items: Upload the driver JAR and enter the connection URL and credentials
Run Test Connection from the source
Enter the account SQL query and discover the account schema
Configure account correlation to the identity attribute
Run account aggregation and review uncorrelated accounts
questions.explanation: Connectivity comes first, then the query and schema that shape accounts, then correlation so the first aggregation links accounts to identities.

questions.stem: Match each connector type to the situation it fits BEST.

pairs.match: An HR system that only produces a CSV export
An in-house app whose users live in an on-premises database
A REST API with no prebuilt SailPoint connector
A cloud app connected without any virtual appliance

targets_extra: A system reached only by reading an email inbox
questions.explanation: Pick the connector that matches how the target stores and exposes identities: files, databases, REST APIs, directories or cloud-native SaaS connectivity.

questions.stem: An AD source will use SSL to the domain controllers. Which TWO items must be in place?
choices: The VAs can reach the domain controllers on TCP 636
The VAs trust the CA that issued the domain controller certificates
The SailPoint cloud can open inbound connections to the domain controllers
IQService is installed on every domain controller
A cloud rule decrypts the LDAP traffic in the tenant
answers: The VAs can reach the domain controllers on TCP 636
The VAs trust the CA that issued the domain controller certificates
questions.explanation: LDAPS needs the port open from the VAs and a trusted certificate chain on them. The cloud never connects inbound, and IQService is not needed for SSL.

questions.stem: During account aggregation of an on-premises AD source, which component connects to the domain controllers?
choices: A tenant microservice calling the controllers directly
The administrator's browser through the Admin UI
The identity profile engine in the SailPoint cloud
The connector service on a VA in the source's cluster
questions.answer: The connector service on a VA in the source's cluster
questions.explanation: The VA connector reads the directory and sends the results outbound to the tenant for processing. The cloud does not call on-premises systems directly.

questions.stem: An engineer aggregates 8,000 accounts from a new HR source, but no identities appear. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The VA cluster has more than one appliance
Optimized aggregation skipped the new accounts
No identity profile uses the source as its authoritative source yet
The source has no entitlement aggregation schedule
questions.answer: No identity profile uses the source as its authoritative source yet
questions.explanation: Identities are created from accounts on an authoritative source tied to an identity profile. Without that profile the accounts stay as accounts.

questions.stem: A helpdesk admin runs Aggregate Account for a user whose account was removed from the source. The account still shows in ISC. Why?
choices: Single-account aggregation deletes accounts only for admins
Account deletions are processed only by full source aggregations
The identity must be in an inactive lifecycle state first
The VA keeps a cached copy that blocks deletion
questions.answer: Account deletions are processed only by full source aggregations
questions.explanation: Single-account aggregation loads changes for one account but does not delete it if missing. A full aggregation handles deletions under the deletion settings.

questions.stem: A source's aggregation is scheduled for 01:00, but it runs an hour off after the clocks change for daylight saving time. What explains this?
choices: Schedules follow the VA cluster's GMT offset and do not shift for daylight saving
Schedules follow each admin's browser time zone
Schedules follow the time zone of the source owner
Schedules always run in the tenant's US time zone
questions.answer: Schedules follow the VA cluster's GMT offset and do not shift for daylight saving
questions.explanation: The aggregation schedule uses the time zone offset set on the connected VA cluster, which does not move with daylight saving. Browser settings play no part.

questions.stem: An app owner wants a non-authoritative source aggregated every hour during the workday. What is the BEST advice?
choices: Aggregate every hour, since more runs keep data safer
Aggregate only when an access request is submitted
Replace aggregation with a weekly certification
Aggregate as rarely as needs allow, usually daily and outside business hours
questions.answer: Aggregate as rarely as needs allow, usually daily and outside business hours
questions.explanation: SailPoint advises aggregating non-authoritative sources rarely, seldom more than once a day, and outside business hours to limit load. Certifications do not refresh account data.

questions.stem: An admin is preparing the first CSV for a new flat file source and needs the expected columns. What should the admin use?
choices: Download Account Schema on the source's account aggregation page
Export the identity profile's mappings as a CSV
Run a search query and export the results
Copy the column names from another source's file
questions.answer: Download Account Schema on the source's account aggregation page
questions.explanation: Download Account Schema gives a template built from the source's account schema. Identity profile mappings describe identity attributes, not the file layout.

questions.stem: After a delimited file import, each account shows only one entitlement although the file lists several rows per account. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Mark the account ID as multi-valued
Upload the file through the VA instead
Sort the file by account ID before uploading it
Turn off account deletion for the source
questions.answer: Sort the file by account ID before uploading it
questions.explanation: Rows for the same account must be together, so the file must be sorted by account ID to merge entitlements. The account ID itself is never multi-valued.

questions.stem: HR identities carry employeeNumber, and the app's accounts carry empId with the same values. How should the engineer correlate them?
choices: Create an access profile that contains empId
Map identity attribute employeeNumber to account attribute empId
Map empId to the identity's display name
Add empId as a lifecycle state
questions.answer: Map identity attribute employeeNumber to account attribute empId
questions.explanation: Correlation compares an identity attribute with an account attribute and links on a match. Access profiles and lifecycle states do not link accounts.

questions.stem: An engineer fixes the correlation settings, but uncorrelated accounts stay uncorrelated after the next scheduled aggregation. What should the engineer do?
choices: Delete and recreate the source
Wait for the nightly identity refresh
Run an unoptimized aggregation through the API
Raise the account deletion threshold
questions.answer: Run an unoptimized aggregation through the API
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation skips unchanged accounts and does not re-evaluate their correlation. An unoptimized run re-evaluates every account; deleting the source loses history.

questions.stem: After aggregation, 200 accounts have no attribute that matches any identity. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Delete all 200 accounts from ISC
Create a new identity for each account
Make the source authoritative
Fix the data where possible and manually correlate the rest
questions.answer: Fix the data where possible and manually correlate the rest
questions.explanation: Uncorrelated accounts should be cleaned up at the source or linked manually, for example with a correlation file. Making the app authoritative would create bad identities.

questions.stem: During an optimized aggregation, which accounts have their correlation evaluated?
choices: New accounts and accounts whose data changed
Every account on the source
Only accounts already correlated
Only accounts flagged by a certification
questions.answer: New accounts and accounts whose data changed
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation skips accounts with no data changes, so correlation and manager correlation run only for new or changed ones.

questions.stem: Which account attribute is the BEST correlation key to an HR identity?
choices: The user's display name
The employee ID that HR also stores
The account's last login date
The user's job title
questions.answer: The employee ID that HR also stores
questions.explanation: A unique, stable value present on both sides gives reliable correlation. Display names repeat and titles change.

questions.stem: Security wants owners to review accounts on several sources that are not linked to any identity. What should the engineer set up?
choices: A role composition certification
A manager certification for all identities
An SoD policy for orphaned accounts
An uncorrelated accounts certification campaign
questions.answer: An uncorrelated accounts certification campaign
questions.explanation: An uncorrelated accounts certification reviews accounts with no owner identity. Manager campaigns only cover accounts already tied to identities.

questions.stem: Account IDs look like E12345 while HR employee numbers are 12345, and a simple attribute match fails. Which option fits BEST?
choices: A connector rule that runs on the IQService host
A correlation rule, which SailPoint reviews before deployment
A lifecycle state that renames the account
A provisioning policy on the source
questions.answer: A correlation rule, which SailPoint reviews before deployment
questions.explanation: A correlation rule is a cloud rule that can apply custom matching logic and must pass SailPoint's rule review. Provisioning policies only build new account values.

questions.stem: What does the default optimized account aggregation do?
choices: Reads only records changed since the last run
Reads every record and reprocesses all of them
Reads every record and skips processing for unchanged accounts
Reads only accounts that are correlated
questions.answer: Reads every record and skips processing for unchanged accounts
questions.explanation: Optimized aggregation still retrieves all records but skips correlation and processing when nothing changed. Reading only changed records is delta aggregation.

questions.stem: A DBA complains that full aggregations overload the database every night. Which option reduces the records read from the source?
choices: Delta aggregation, where the source supports it
Optimized aggregation, which is already the default
Unoptimized aggregation through the API
A higher deletion threshold
questions.answer: Delta aggregation, where the source supports it
questions.explanation: Delta aggregation loads only changed, added or removed records. Optimized aggregation still reads every record, so the database load stays the same.

questions.stem: An engineer needs every account on a direct source reprocessed after changing manager correlation. How is that done?
choices: Start Aggregation in the Admin UI twice
Schedule the aggregation for midnight
Call the load-accounts API with disableOptimization set to true
Enable delta aggregation on the source
questions.answer: Call the load-accounts API with disableOptimization set to true
questions.explanation: Unoptimized aggregation is triggered through the API with disableOptimization, and only for that run. UI aggregations always run optimized.

questions.stem: A faulty HR export contains half the usual rows. What protects identities from mass deletion during aggregation?
choices: Optimized aggregation, which ignores missing accounts
The identity profile priority setting
The cluster's second VA
The percentage of deleted accounts allowed, which cancels the run
questions.answer: The percentage of deleted accounts allowed, which cancels the run
questions.explanation: When deletions would exceed the allowed percentage, the aggregation is canceled and a warning is raised. Optimization does not stop deletions.

questions.stem: A source has 10 accounts and the percentage of deleted accounts allowed is 3%. What is the risk?
choices: The value rounds to zero accounts, so only a 100% deletion cancels the run
Every aggregation is canceled because 3% is too strict
Deleted accounts are kept forever as hidden accounts
The threshold is ignored for small sources
questions.answer: The value rounds to zero accounts, so only a 100% deletion cancels the run
questions.explanation: On small sources the value rounds to whole accounts; if it does not reach one account, the run is canceled only if all accounts would go. Set it to represent at least one account.

questions.stem: Accounts removed from a source still show in ISC after full aggregations. What is the MOST likely setting?
choices: Delta aggregation is turned on for the source
Enable Account Deletion is turned off for the source
The source uses a SaaS connector
Correlation is set on employee ID
questions.answer: Enable Account Deletion is turned off for the source
questions.explanation: Accounts missing from the source are deleted only when account deletion is enabled. Correlation settings do not control deletion.

questions.stem: A leaver's HR account is deleted during aggregation, but the identity owns an access profile and has no other authoritative account. What happens to the identity?
choices: It stays as a hidden identity because ownership blocks deletion
It moves to the inactive lifecycle state and stays visible
It is deleted immediately along with the access profile
It is reassigned to the source owner's identity profile
questions.answer: It stays as a hidden identity because ownership blocks deletion
questions.explanation: Deletion is blocked for identities that own objects such as access profiles, so the identity remains hidden. Reassignment happens only with another authoritative account.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: An HR database holds 20 years of former staff. Only current workers and recent leavers belong in ISC. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Aggregate every row and delete the old ones in ISC
Aggregate every row and hide old identities with a lifecycle state
Export only old rows to a separate flat file source
Add a WHERE clause to the account query so other rows never leave the database
questions.answer: Add a WHERE clause to the account query so other rows never leave the database
questions.explanation: Filtering in the query keeps out-of-scope data from ever reaching the cloud. Deleting or hiding after aggregation still sends the data.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: Service accounts in a dedicated AD OU should not reach the tenant at all. What is the BEST control?
choices: Aggregate them and leave them uncorrelated
Aggregate them and certify them quarterly
Exclude that OU through the account search DN or search filter
Aggregate them and remove their entitlements
questions.answer: Exclude that OU through the account search DN or search filter
questions.explanation: Scoping the search keeps the objects on premises. Leaving them uncorrelated still stores them in the tenant.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: A SaaS application returns a national ID number with every user, and no one needs it in ISC. What is the BEST step?
choices: Map the attribute to a hidden identity attribute
Remove the attribute from the source's account schema
Add a transform that uppercases the attribute
Create an access profile that excludes the attribute
questions.answer: Remove the attribute from the source's account schema
questions.explanation: Attributes not in the account schema are not collected or stored. Mapping it to an identity attribute would spread the data further.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: According to SailPoint aggregation best practice, how should engineers limit the records they aggregate?
choices: Use filtering on the connector to bring in only needed records
Aggregate everything and filter in search
Aggregate everything and rely on certifications
Aggregate everything and set a high deletion threshold
questions.answer: Use filtering on the connector to bring in only needed records
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends connector-side filtering so only important, current records are aggregated. Filtering in search still stores everything.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: Why is filtering at the source query BETTER than removing unwanted accounts after they reach ISC?
choices: Filtering at the source turns on encryption at rest
Unwanted data never leaves the network and aggregation does less work
Filtering at the source removes the need for a VA
Filtering at the source makes every account authoritative
questions.answer: Unwanted data never leaves the network and aggregation does less work
questions.explanation: Source-side filters keep data on premises and shrink every run. Encryption at rest applies to tenant data whatever the filter.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: A Web Services source pulls all users from an API that supports a status filter, but only active users are needed. What should the engineer change?
choices: Add a lifecycle state for inactive users
Add a role that removes inactive users
Add a second cluster for inactive users
Add the status filter to the aggregation HTTP operation's request
questions.answer: Add the status filter to the aggregation HTTP operation's request
questions.explanation: Filtering in the API request means inactive users are never returned. Lifecycle states and roles act after the data is already in ISC.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: A flat file export for a disconnected app includes bank account columns that ISC does not use. What is the BEST action?
choices: Upload the file and restrict the source to Source Admins
Upload the file and exclude it from search
Remove the unneeded columns from the file before uploading it
Upload the file and enable account deletion
questions.answer: Remove the unneeded columns from the file before uploading it
questions.explanation: Data in an uploaded file goes straight to the tenant, so unneeded columns should be stripped first. Restricting admin access still stores the data.

questions.stem: An auditor asks whether virtual appliances keep a permanent store of aggregated identity data. What is the BEST answer?
choices: Yes, each VA keeps a full replica of the tenant
No, VAs move data to the tenant, which is where it is stored
Yes, VAs store data so the cloud can read it later
No, aggregated data stays only on the source system
questions.answer: No, VAs move data to the tenant, which is where it is stored
questions.explanation: The VA connects to sources and sends results to the tenant; the tenant is the system of record. Data is stored in the cloud, not only on the source.

questions.stem: A European company must keep identity data stored in the EU. What is the BEST way to meet this?
choices: Deploy all VAs in an EU data center
Use only flat file sources
Have the tenant provisioned in a SailPoint EU region
Turn off search for EU identities
questions.answer: Have the tenant provisioned in a SailPoint EU region
questions.explanation: Data is stored in the region where the tenant is hosted. VA location only affects where connectors run, not where the tenant keeps data.

questions.stem: An account attribute that does not affect any identity changed during aggregation, but Search still shows the old value hours later. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: Such changes reach Search through a nightly sync that can take up to 24 hours
The aggregation failed and must be rerun
The VA cached the old value permanently
Search only shows authoritative source data
questions.answer: Such changes reach Search through a nightly sync that can take up to 24 hours
questions.explanation: Changes that affect identities appear in Search quickly, but other updates can wait for the nightly synchronization job. The aggregation itself succeeded.

questions.stem: Where are the credentials of a VA-based source kept after an admin saves them?
choices: On the admin's browser in local storage
In plain text on the source configuration page
On the target system's own credential vault
In the tenant, encrypted so only the cluster's VAs can decrypt them
questions.answer: In the tenant, encrypted so only the cluster's VAs can decrypt them
questions.explanation: Source credentials are stored encrypted with the VA cluster's key, so only those VAs can use them. They are not kept in the browser or in plain text.

questions.stem: A team wants to know whether a delimited file source needs a virtual appliance to load data. What is correct?
choices: Yes, every source must be assigned to a VA cluster
No, the file is uploaded to the tenant without a VA
Yes, the VA parses the file before it is stored
No, the file is emailed to SailPoint support
questions.answer: No, the file is uploaded to the tenant without a VA
questions.explanation: Delimited file data is uploaded directly to the tenant, so no VA is involved. VAs are needed for connectors that reach systems in private networks.

questions.stem: An admin needs to review aggregation runs across all sources from the past two months. Where should the admin look?
choices: Admin > Connections > Aggregation Activity, which keeps 90 days
The VA's local log folder only
The identity profile's preview page
The source's provisioning policy
questions.answer: Admin > Connections > Aggregation Activity, which keeps 90 days
questions.explanation: Aggregation Activity lists aggregations from the past 90 days across sources. VA logs rotate and cover only that appliance.

questions.stem: Put the stages of an account aggregation for a VA-based authoritative source in order.
items: The tenant queues the aggregation task for the source's VA cluster
A VA's connector reads the accounts from the source system
The VA sends the account data outbound to the tenant
The tenant compares accounts with existing data and correlates them
Identity attributes and lifecycle states are recalculated for changed identities
questions.explanation: The task goes to the VA, the connector reads the source and sends data to the cloud, and the tenant processes accounts before updating identities.

questions.topic: Filtering Data Sent to the Cloud
questions.stem: A source holds a sensitive column and many former staff that ISC does not need. Which TWO steps keep that data out of the cloud?
choices: Leave the column out of the query and the account schema
Filter out former staff in the source query or search filter
Map the column to an identity attribute that admins cannot see
Place the VA in a separate network segment
Raise the percentage of deleted accounts allowed
answers: Leave the column out of the query and the account schema
Filter out former staff in the source query or search filter
questions.explanation: Data that is never queried or matched never leaves the source. Mapping it to an identity attribute still stores it, and VA placement does not filter data.

questions.stem: Match each aggregation type to what it does.

pairs.match: Reads all records but skips unchanged accounts
Reads only records changed since the last run
Reloads one account without syncing identity attributes

targets_extra: Deletes missing accounts regardless of the deletion threshold
questions.explanation: Optimized is the default, unoptimized is forced through the API, delta needs source support, and single-account aggregation refreshes one account only.

questions.stem: A disconnected application has no API. Provisioning must be done by a fulfillment team that works ServiceNow tickets. What should the engineer configure?
choices: A ServiceNow Service Catalog integration for the application
A Web Services source pointed at ServiceNow
A JDBC source pointed at the ServiceNow database
A service desk integration attached to the application's source
questions.answer: A service desk integration attached to the application's source
questions.explanation: A service desk integration turns ISC provisioning for the attached source into service desk tickets. The Service Catalog integration lets users request access from ServiceNow instead.

questions.stem: Employees already use the ServiceNow portal and want to request ISC-governed access there. Which integration fits BEST?
choices: The ServiceNow Service Catalog integration
A service desk integration for each source
A ServiceNow connector source for ServiceNow groups
A flat file source loaded from ServiceNow
questions.answer: The ServiceNow Service Catalog integration
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog integration exposes ISC access in the ServiceNow portal while ISC handles approvals and provisioning. A service desk integration only raises fulfillment tickets.

questions.stem: The goal is to aggregate ServiceNow's own users, groups and roles and certify them. What is needed?
choices: A service desk integration for ServiceNow
The ServiceNow Service Catalog integration
A ServiceNow source using SailPoint's ServiceNow connector
A workflow that emails ServiceNow admins
questions.answer: A ServiceNow source using SailPoint's ServiceNow connector
questions.explanation: Managing ServiceNow accounts and groups needs a source with the ServiceNow connector. A service desk integration creates tickets and does not aggregate ServiceNow accounts.

questions.stem: A small app has no API and the company has no service desk tool. How can access changes for it still be tracked in ISC?
choices: A service desk integration with no target system
Manual work items assigned to the source owner
A Web Services source with empty operations
An access profile marked as disconnected
questions.answer: Manual work items assigned to the source owner
questions.explanation: Without a connector or service desk, ISC creates manual tasks for the source owner. A service desk integration needs a real ticketing system.

questions.stem: A team wants only account creation on a source sent to ServiceNow, with disables handled another way. What should the engineer know?
choices: The integration can be limited to create operations only
Once attached, all provisioning operations for that source become tickets
Disables are never sent to a service desk
The source must be authoritative to use tickets
questions.answer: Once attached, all provisioning operations for that source become tickets
questions.explanation: Attaching a source to a service desk integration sends every provisioning operation, including create, modify, enable, disable and delete, as tickets. It cannot be split by operation.

questions.stem: Before ISC can raise ServiceNow tickets through a service desk integration, what is typically needed on the ServiceNow side?
choices: A VA installed inside the ServiceNow instance
A ServiceNow-hosted copy of the identity profile
A ServiceNow rule reviewed by SailPoint
SailPoint's service desk app and a catalog item for the tickets
questions.answer: SailPoint's service desk app and a catalog item for the tickets
questions.explanation: ServiceNow needs the SailPoint service desk application and a catalog item that ISC raises tickets against. No VA is installed in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: An app gains a documented provisioning API. It is currently fulfilled by service desk tickets. What is the BEST long-term design?
choices: Move it to a direct connector so provisioning is automated
Keep tickets, because direct connectors cannot be certified
Add a second service desk integration for redundancy
Change it to a flat file source with manual tasks
questions.answer: Move it to a direct connector so provisioning is automated
questions.explanation: Service desk integrations suit systems that cannot be provisioned automatically. When an API exists, a direct connector removes manual delay and errors.

questions.stem: ServiceNow tickets are closed by fulfillers, but the matching ISC requests stay pending. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source's account deletion threshold is too low
The VA cluster is in the wrong time zone
The closed ticket status is not mapped to a completed ISC status
The identity profile priority is set incorrectly
questions.answer: The closed ticket status is not mapped to a completed ISC status
questions.explanation: ISC reads the ticket status and relies on the status mapping to know a ticket is done. An unmapped status leaves the request waiting.

questions.stem: How does ISC learn that a service desk ticket it created has been completed?
choices: It checks the ticket status and translates it through the status mapping
The fulfiller completes a matching work item in ISC
The VA scans the service desk database each night
An identity refresh closes all open tickets
questions.answer: It checks the ticket status and translates it through the status mapping
questions.explanation: The integration checks ticket status in the service desk and maps it to ISC statuses. Fulfillers work in the service desk, not in ISC.

questions.stem: A ticket for a new account on a flat file source is closed. When does the new account show on the identity in ISC?
choices: Immediately when the ticket closes
After the next aggregation of that source's data
Only after a manager certification
Only after the identity changes lifecycle state
questions.answer: After the next aggregation of that source's data
questions.explanation: Closing the ticket tells ISC the work is done, but the account data arrives through the source's next aggregation. Certifications do not load accounts.

questions.stem: Fulfillers want each ticket to show the requested entitlement and the identity's manager. Where is this BEST configured?
choices: In the account schema of the flat file source
In the identity profile's attribute mappings
In the VA cluster's configuration file
In the ticket template of the integration's provisioning settings
questions.answer: In the ticket template of the integration's provisioning settings
questions.explanation: The service desk integration's provisioning settings build the ticket fields from the provisioning request. The account schema describes accounts, not tickets.

questions.stem: Five disconnected applications must all be fulfilled through the same ServiceNow instance. What is the simplest design?
choices: Five ServiceNow instances, one per source
Five Web Services sources calling ServiceNow
One service desk integration with all five sources attached
One flat file source holding all five applications
questions.answer: One service desk integration with all five sources attached
questions.explanation: A single integration can serve several sources, and its templates can route tickets. Merging apps into one source would lose per-app ownership.

questions.stem: Access requests on a ticketed source fail, and the integration reports HTTP 401 from ServiceNow when creating tickets. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The integration user's credentials in the service desk configuration
The source's account deletion threshold
The firewall between the VA and the domain controllers
The identity profile's lifecycle states
questions.answer: The integration user's credentials in the service desk configuration
questions.explanation: A 401 means ServiceNow rejected the integration's authentication. Deletion thresholds and DC firewalls are unrelated.

questions.stem: After attaching a source to a service desk integration, the source owner says they no longer get provisioning tasks in ISC. What is happening?
choices: The integration has failed and dropped the requests
The source owner lost the Source Admin user level
ISC now provisions the source directly
The work now goes to service desk tickets instead of ISC tasks
questions.answer: The work now goes to service desk tickets instead of ISC tasks
questions.explanation: With a service desk attached, provisioning becomes tickets for the fulfillment team. Manual work items are for sources with no other channel.

questions.stem: A new source fails its first aggregation. What should the engineer do FIRST?
choices: Delete the VA cluster and build a new one
Run Test Connection on the source and read the returned error
Open a ticket with SailPoint before testing
Change the source to a flat file
questions.answer: Run Test Connection on the source and read the returned error
questions.explanation: Test Connection checks the VA's path and credentials to the target and returns a specific error to work from. Rebuilding the cluster is drastic and premature.

questions.stem: An engineer needs the detailed connector stack trace for a failing AD source. Which file on the VA is the BEST place to look?
choices: /etc/hosts
/home/sailpoint/config.yaml
/home/sailpoint/log/ccg.log
/var/log/boot.log
questions.answer: /home/sailpoint/log/ccg.log
questions.explanation: ccg.log holds the connector gateway's messages, including connector errors and stack traces. config.yaml holds VA settings, not runtime errors.

questions.stem: Every source on one VA cluster suddenly fails Test Connection, and the cluster shows unhealthy. What is the MOST likely area to investigate?
choices: The account schema of each source
The correlation settings of each source
The VAs' outbound connection to the SailPoint tenant
The identity profile mappings
questions.answer: The VAs' outbound connection to the SailPoint tenant
questions.explanation: When all sources on a cluster fail together, the shared path from the VAs to the cloud is the likely problem. Schema or correlation issues affect one source at a time.

questions.stem: Only one JDBC source fails on a cluster where every other source works. Where is the problem MOST likely?
choices: The VAs' outbound connection to the tenant
The cluster's keyPassphrase
The tenant's encryption at rest
The path or credentials between the VAs and that database
questions.answer: The path or credentials between the VAs and that database
questions.explanation: If other sources on the same cluster work, the VA-to-cloud link is fine, so the issue is specific to that target. A passphrase problem would affect every source.

questions.stem: After changing a source's settings, aggregations keep failing as if the old settings were still in use. What is a documented fix?
choices: Clear the cached jobs on each VA and reboot them one at a time
Delete the source and its accounts
Reboot all VAs in the cluster at once
Raise the account deletion threshold
questions.answer: Clear the cached jobs on each VA and reboot them one at a time
questions.explanation: Cached jobs on a VA can hold old connector settings; clearing them and rebooting each VA in turn makes them reload configuration. Rebooting all at once causes an outage.

questions.stem: Aggregations on a supported source fail now and then with "Connection Reset". Which source attributes can the engineer set to control retries?
choices: searchDN, iterateSearchFilter and groupSearchDN
aggregationRetryErrors, retryWaitTime and maxRetryCount
keyPassphrase, clusterName and timeZone
accountQuery, getObjectSQL and groupQuery
questions.answer: aggregationRetryErrors, retryWaitTime and maxRetryCount
questions.explanation: These connector attributes list the errors to retry, the wait between tries and the number of tries. The others are search, VA or SQL settings.

questions.stem: Aggregation of a slow source stops with a timeout although the connection works. What can the engineer adjust through the API?
choices: The source's aggregateTimeout connector attribute
The VA cluster's time zone setting
The identity profile's priority
The source's account deletion percentage
questions.answer: The source's aggregateTimeout connector attribute
questions.explanation: aggregateTimeout, set in the source's connector attributes, gives the aggregation more time, in seconds. Time zone and priority have nothing to do with timeouts.

questions.stem: Test Connection returns java.net.UnknownHostException for the database host. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The database rejected the service account password
The VA cannot resolve the host name through DNS
The database certificate has expired
The account query has a syntax error
questions.answer: The VA cannot resolve the host name through DNS
questions.explanation: UnknownHostException means the name could not be resolved, so check DNS from the VA and the host name spelling. A bad password gives a login error.

questions.stem: Test Connection fails with "Connection refused" to a domain controller. What does this MOST likely mean?
choices: DNS could not find the domain controller
A firewall silently dropped the packets
The host answered, but nothing is listening on that port
The service account is locked
questions.answer: The host answered, but nothing is listening on that port
questions.explanation: Refused means the host actively rejected the connection, often a wrong port or stopped service. Silent drops usually show as timeouts instead.

questions.stem: A JDBC source shows "connect timed out" while DNS resolves correctly. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The JDBC driver JAR is missing
The SQL login password is wrong
The account query returns no rows
A firewall between the VA and the database is dropping traffic
questions.answer: A firewall between the VA and the database is dropping traffic
questions.explanation: A timeout with good DNS points to traffic being dropped on the network path. A missing driver or bad password returns its own error quickly.

questions.stem: An AD source using SSL fails with "PKIX path building failed". What should the engineer do?
choices: Turn off SSL and use plain LDAP for provisioning
Add the issuing CA certificate, in PEM format, to the VAs' certificates folder
Reset the service account password
Lower the account deletion threshold
questions.answer: Add the issuing CA certificate, in PEM format, to the VAs' certificates folder
questions.explanation: That error means the VA does not trust the server's certificate chain, so the CA certificate goes in /home/sailpoint/certificates. Turning off SSL would break password resets.

questions.stem: After a CA certificate was added, an LDAPS source works on some aggregations and fails with certificate errors on others. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The certificate was added to only one VA in the cluster
The certificate is in PEM format
The source lists more than one domain controller
Delta aggregation is turned on
questions.answer: The certificate was added to only one VA in the cluster
questions.explanation: Any VA in the cluster can run the task, so each one must trust the certificate. PEM is the expected format.

questions.stem: An LDAPS source configured with a DC's IP address fails with a certificate name mismatch. The certificate is issued to dc01.corp.example.com. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Reissue the certificate without any subject name
Disable certificate checks on the VA
Configure the source with the host name that is on the certificate
Move the source to a new VA cluster
questions.answer: Configure the source with the host name that is on the certificate
questions.explanation: TLS checks that the name used to connect matches the certificate, so use the FQDN it names. Disabling checks weakens security.

questions.stem: Large aggregations intermittently fail with "Read timed out" while small tests pass. What is a likely cause?
choices: An invalid keyPassphrase on the VA
A missing identity profile
An expired SailPoint license
Network latency or slow processing on the source server
questions.answer: Network latency or slow processing on the source server
questions.explanation: Read timeouts on large runs point to latency, network devices or a slow source, which retries and timeouts can absorb. A bad passphrase would fail every task.

questions.stem: An AD source returns LDAP error 49 with data 52e. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The service account is locked out
The service account's password has expired
The domain controller is unreachable
The service account's user name or password is wrong
questions.answer: The service account's user name or password is wrong
questions.explanation: Code 49 with 52e means invalid credentials. A locked account shows 775 and an expired password shows 532.

questions.stem: An AD source suddenly fails with LDAP error 49, data 775, after someone tested the service account. What happened?
choices: The service account password is wrong
The service account was deleted
The service account is locked out
The domain controller's certificate expired
questions.answer: The service account is locked out
questions.explanation: Data 775 means the account is locked, often from repeated bad sign-ins. Unlocking it and fixing the cause restores the connection.

questions.stem: An AD source that worked for months fails with LDAP error 49, data 532. What should the engineer do?
choices: Unlock the service account in AD
Update the expired service account password in AD and on the source
Add the CA certificate to the VAs
Open the Global Catalog port
questions.answer: Update the expired service account password in AD and on the source
questions.explanation: Data 532 means the password has expired. The new password must be set in AD and updated on the source.

questions.stem: Aggregation from AD works, but creating users fails with "insufficient access rights". What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The service account lacks write rights on the target OU
The VA cannot resolve the domain name
The domain controller certificate is untrusted
The account search DN is too narrow
questions.answer: The service account lacks write rights on the target OU
questions.explanation: Reading works but writing fails, so the account needs create and modify rights where users are created. Network or certificate problems would also break aggregation.

questions.stem: A JDBC source for SQL Server fails with "Login failed for user". What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: The DNS records for the database host
The firewall rule for the database port
The JDBC driver JAR version
The database credentials and whether SQL logins are allowed
questions.answer: The database credentials and whether SQL logins are allowed
questions.explanation: A login failure means the server was reached and rejected the credentials or login type. DNS or firewall problems would stop the connection earlier.

questions.stem: A Web Services source gets HTTP 403 on its aggregation call, while the token request succeeds. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The API client's secret is wrong
The VA cannot resolve the API host
The API client lacks the permission or scope for that endpoint
The account schema is missing an attribute
questions.answer: The API client lacks the permission or scope for that endpoint
questions.explanation: 403 means the caller authenticated but is not allowed to use the endpoint. A wrong secret would fail the token request with 401.

questions.stem: Match each connection error to its MOST likely cause.

pairs.match: The VA cannot resolve the host name
Nothing is listening on the target port
A firewall is dropping the traffic
The VA does not trust the server certificate
The service account credentials are wrong

targets_extra: The identity profile priority is too low
questions.explanation: Each error points at a different layer: name resolution, the listening service, the network path, certificate trust or authentication.

questions.stem: An LDAPS source fails Test Connection with a certificate trust error. Put the fix in order.
items: Read the PKIX error in Test Connection and ccg.log
Export the issuing CA certificate in PEM format
Copy the certificate to /home/sailpoint/certificates on every VA in the cluster
Restart the connector service on each VA so it loads the certificate
questions.explanation: Confirm the cause, add the CA certificate to every VA in the cluster, let the VAs load it, then retest.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about a ServiceNow service desk integration in ISC are correct?
choices: All provisioning operations for an attached source become tickets
ISC checks ticket status and maps it to the request status
It aggregates ServiceNow's own users and groups
It lets users request ISC access from the ServiceNow portal
It must run on a VA installed inside ServiceNow
answers: All provisioning operations for an attached source become tickets
ISC checks ticket status and maps it to the request status
questions.explanation: The integration turns provisioning into tickets and tracks their status. Aggregating ServiceNow needs its connector, and portal requests need the Service Catalog integration.
